verdict.rationale: ROS 2 ships its own credential mechanism through SROS2. You create a keystore with `ros2 security create_keystore`, and each security enclave encapsulates a single policy for protecting communications, with participant authentication and control over communications across the ROS graph. That makes per-participant, policy-scoped credentials plausible for a node acting as an agent. However, the evidence never shows fine-grained least-privilege permissions such as per-topic or per-service allow/deny, and it says nothing about agent-oriented credential issuance or API tokens. Missing for 10: documented per-topic/service permission scoping, credential issuance framed for AI agents, revocation/expiry of scoped credentials, independent or hands-on corroboration.
